plates.notes: Davioud's block at the Seine end of the boulevard. 5 regular bays, very even pitch (3.22 m). Masonry facade is rez + entresol (both inside one shopfront frame) + 1er + 2e + 3e; above the cornice a brick-faced comble carrying a FULL storey of stone-dressed windows with iron garde-corps plus an attic band of small square windows. That comble is 7.0 m - 28.5% of total height - which is the largest comble fraction in this group by a wide margin and is the number to look at if the generator's comble-fill constant is being calibrated. Window aspect is remarkably constant across storeys (h/w 1.81-1.94) even as storey height falls. Two entrances (Nos 2 and 4); the left/major one was measured.

plates.notes: The tightest-grained facade in the group: SIX bays on 14.75 m, so a bay pitch of only 2.35 m (pitch/width 0.16). Balcons filants at every one of the four upper storeys - this is a facade whose ironwork does the decorative work. Storey taper 1er->2e->3e is clean and monotonic (3.48 / 3.04 / 2.87 m) but the 4e recovers to 2.99 m, the same non-monotonic top-storey behaviour seen on plate 01. The cornice band itself is very shallow here and I could not separate its lower edge from the window pediments below, so the top storey height is quoted to cornice TOP and is ~0.15-0.3 m generous.

plates.notes: The rue de Rivoli type and the outlier of the group: NO mansard. The roof is flat/concealed behind a balustrade and the storey above the main cornice is a masonry attic with louvered shutters fronted by a balcon filant. Only 4.85 m of very tall boutique rez, then a LOW arched 1er (2.97 m) under a tall 2e piano nobile (3.87 m) - the taper is inverted between those two, exactly as at plate 34. Also the only porte cochere in the group that reaches a full bay width (2.58 m x 3.64 m). Height to cornice is only 14.8 m, well under the legal maximum: this building spends its allowance on fewer, taller storeys. Facade extent is UNCERTAIN because the plate draws the flanking neighbours; the symmetry axis at x=925.5 is however unambiguous.

plates.notes: Six bays on 17.35 m. Composition: tall boutique rez (4.20 m), a LOW rusticated 1er (3.10 m), then the piano nobile 2e (4.29 m) with the richest window frames, then a monotonic taper 3.70 / 2.89 m. Balcon filant only at the 4e; balconets elsewhere. Opening aspect ratio tracks the hierarchy strongly here - h/w runs 1.90 / 2.45 / 2.06 / 1.62 from 1er to 4e, i.e. the noble floor's windows are markedly the most slender and the top floor's the squattest and WIDEST in plan. Comble 4.32 m = 18.4% of total. Height to cornice 19.2 m, again close to the 20 m maximum.
